items.title: Bill Crow interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: Joseph Mitchell was another of my great heroes. He wrote articles about New York for the New Yorker and his stuff is now collected in a wonderful book. But unfortunately he hasn’t written anything. He’s still around but he hasn’t written anything for quite a while.

ctx.x: Yeah, well, I’ve always been interested in writing. I was a big reader when I was a kid, I learned to read before I started grade school. My mother had a little primer and she taught me at home. She also taught me to sing and I guess I inherited my musical ears from her. She was a musician. But I can remember standing by her ironing board singing songs with her before I could see up over the ironing board, so I know I was pretty young. And she tells me that when I still used to take naps in the afternoon in my…

things saw me as a prized student. So they fed me stuff. I think it was a sixth grade teacher that gave me copies of the New Yorker, which I’d never seen before. And I fell in love with James Thurber and E.B. White and Alexander Wolcott, and became quite a sophisticate for the small town that we were in. Some of the terms I didn’t understand at all, I had to go find out what they were talking about, but that was my beginning of my appreciation of really good writing. And I think E.B. White became my hero because…
Did this influence your eventually coming to New York?
